Single Quantiles of a Quantile Grid

Source: R/split_quantile_grid.R
split_quantile_grid.Rd

Splits a structural quantile VAR, a model created with quantile_grid = TRUE in create_bvarmodel, into one model per quantile.

Usage

split_quantile_grid(object)

Arguments

object

an object of class 'bvarmodel' holding a grid of quantiles, usually the result of a call to add_posterior_coefficients.

Value

A list of class 'modellist' with one object of class 'bvarmodel' per quantile, in increasing order.

Details

The draws of a grid are stacked level by level, and each level's draws are the chain the single-quantile model would have drawn. The models returned hold those draws with the specification of that model, so that everything written for a single quantile – summary, plot, add_posterior_loglik – reads them as such. What describes the grid as a whole, its forecasts and its log likelihood, is not carried over. The impulse responses of a structural grid are differences of forecasts at a fixed level with and without a scenario; see forecast_quantile in add_posterior_forecasts.

See also

create_bvarmodel

Other post-estimation analysis: add_sign_restrictions.bvarmodel(), add_sign_zero_restrictions.bvarmodel(), fevd.bvarmodel(), fevd.bvecmodel(), historical_decomposition(), historical_decomposition.bvarmodel(), irf.bvarmodel(), irf.bvecmodel(), multipliers(), multipliers.bvarmodel(), multipliers.bvecmodel(), predict.bvarmodel(), spillover.bvarmodel(), spillover.bvecmodel(), vec_to_var.bvecmodel()

Examples


data("us_macrodata")

object <- create_bvarmodel(data = us_macrodata, p = 1, deterministic = "const",
                           structural = TRUE, error = "ald",
                           quantile = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), quantile_grid = TRUE,
                           iterations = 20, burnin = 10)
object <- add_priors(object, coef = list(v_i = 1),
                     sigma = list(shape = 3, rate = .01))
object <- add_initial_values(object)
object <- add_posterior_coefficients(object)

levels <- split_quantile_grid(object)
summary(levels[[3]])
